utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Case number IT-05-86-I, the Prosecutor versus Milorad Trbic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the appearances, please. For the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. My name is Peter McCloskey and with me today is Lise-Lotte Karlsson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the appearances for the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour, Eugene O'Sullivan, appearing for Mr. Trbic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to greet everyone present, members of the Prosecution, Defence counsel for the accused, and the accused. I would first like to ask the accused to stand up and to tell me whether he is receiving the interpretation of what I am saying into his own language.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may sit down now. I would first like to remind you of the background of the indictment. On the 7th of April, 2005 the accused was transferred to the Tribunal's Detention Unit by an order dated the 24th of March, 2005. Judge Liu confirmed the indictment on the 10th of February, 2005 brought against the accused Pandurevic and the accused who is present in the courtroom, the accused Milorad Trbic. The indictment states that at the beginning of July, 1995, Drina Corps units of the Bosnian Serb army shelled Srebrenica and shelled UN observation posts located in the safe haven which was held by Dutch forces. VRS forces then entered into Srebrenica. The indictment alleges that between the 11th and 18th of July, 1995, and I quote: Forces of the VRS, under the command and control of Ratko Mladic, Radislav Krstic, and Vinko Pandurevic expelled and killed a significant part of the Muslim population of Bosnia in the Srebrenica enclave. Milorad Trbic, a security officer of the Zvornik Brigade under the command of Vinko Pandurevic took part in the organisation on the reception, detention, and killing of thousands of Muslim men of Bosnia who had been transported to the zone of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade from the 13th to the 17th of July, 1995. And he personally executed Muslim men from Srebrenica in Orahovac during this period. By their actions, the VRS forces thus practically eliminated all Muslim presence in Bosnia in the Srebrenica enclave and pursued in this manner the campaign of ethnic cleansing that had commenced in the spring of 1992. According to the indictment brought against the accused, who is present here, Milorad Trbic, the accused was an assistant to left Drago Nikolic, the security chief of the Zvornik Brigade and he was directly subordinated to him. Milorad Trbic held the rank of reserve captain. The indictment states that Milorad Trbic is accused on the basis of individual criminal responsibility pursuant to Article 7(1) of the statute of the Tribunal. He has been accused on a single count, a count of crime against humanity, Article 5 of the statute, murder. This is count 4 in the indictment. By order of the President dated the 8th of April, 2005, this case was assigned to Trial Chamber two and as a Judge in that chamber. On the 8th of April, 2005 I was designated as the judge for the purposes of the Initial Appearance. Pursuant to rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, I would like to ask Milorad Trbic to rise and to answer a few questions that I shall put to him. Sir, for the record, could you please tell me your first and last name.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Milorad Trbic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you tell me your date of birth and place of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was born on the 22nd of February, 1958 in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you tell me what you are by profession.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I worked in the Zenica iron works as someone involved in the field of energy, energetics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, given your status of an accused, you have a certain number of rights, which we will now inform you of. The registrar will now read out to you Articles 20 and 21 of the Statute of this Tribunal. Registrar, could you please read out the Articles referred to.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. "Commencement and conduct of trial proceedings. Trial Chamber shall ensure that a trial is fair and expeditious and that proceedings are conducted in accordance with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, with full respect for the rights of the accused and due regard for the protection of victims and witnesses. "A person against whom an indictment has been confirmed shall, pursuant to an order or an arrest warrant of International Tribunal, be taken into custody, immediately informed of the charges against him and transferred to the International Tribunal. The Trial Chamber shall read the indictment, satisfy itself that the rights of the Accused are respected, confirm that the accused understands the indictment, and instruct the Accused to enter a plea. The Trial Chamber shall then set the date of the trial. "The hearings shall be public, unless the Trial Chamber decides to close the proceedings in accordance with its Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Article 21 reads as follows: "Rights of the accused. "1, all persons shall be equal before the international Tribunal. "2, in the determination of charges against him, the Accused shall be entitled to a fair and public hearing, subject to article 22 of the statute. "3. The accused shall be presumed innocent unless proved guilty, according to the provisions of the present statute. "4. In the determination of any charge against the accused pursuant to the present statute, the accused shall be entitled to the following minimum guarantees in fully equality. "A, to be informed promptly and in detail in a language which he understand of the nature cause of the charge against him. "B, to have adequate time and facilities for the preparation of his Defence and to communicate with counsel of his own choosing. "C, to be tried without undue delay. "D, to be tried in his presence and to defend himself in person or through legal assistance of his own choosing, to be informed if he does not have legal assistance of his -- of this right and to have legal assistance assigned to him in any case where the interest of justice so require and without payment by him, in any such case, if he does not have sufficient means to pay for it. "E. To examine or have examined the witness against him and to obtain the attendance and examination of witnesses on his behalf under the same conditions as witness against him. "F. To have the free assistance of an interpreter if he cannot understand or speak the language used in the International Tribunal. "G. Not to be compelled to testify against himself or to confess guilt." [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Trbic, have you understood the rights that have just been read out to you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, have you received a copy of the indictment in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you understood the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, would you like to be provided with additional information on the indictment, or do you believe that the information you've been provided with to date is sufficient?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not require any additional information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, pursuant to Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure, we should read out the entire indictment to you, but if you are familiar with the indictment and if you have understood it, it is possible for you to waive this right pursuant to the Rule that I have referred to. Would you like this indictment to be read out to you. I will ask Defence counsel for Defence point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I have met with Mr. Trbic and it is his wish to remain silent today and to enter his plea within 30 days of today's date. So there is no requirement to read the indictment today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Mr. Trbic, your Defence, who is present in the courtroom, has just informed me that you have decided to wait for a 30-day period before informing us of your decision, before informing us of the plea you will be making. Is that what you wish to do?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, we will schedule a hearing which will take place in 30 days time and at that hearing you may enter a plea of guilty or not guilty. Is there anything the Prosecution would like to say at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is there anything Defence counsel would like to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The very last issue that must be dealt with concerns conditions in the Detention Unit. Are the conditions in the Detention Unit satisfactory? Have you run into any difficulties? Are there any problems you would like to inform me of?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am content.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In that case, we will now adjourn. You may sit down sir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I have said, there will be a hearing pursuant to Rule 62, at which the accused may enter a plea. Thank you. And I will inform you of the schedule for the next hearing.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Initial Appearance adjourned at
